results: 1. distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side): POSITIVE - the tremor decreases or stops when the left arm performs a task such as drinking from a cup
2. entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm): POSITIVE - amplitude falls and the rhythm becomes irregular under repetitive voluntary movement of the other side
3. co-activation sign on passive movement of the affected limb: POSITIVE - movement of the contralateral arm co-activates the hand with an increase in tremor intensity
4. 'whack-a-mole' sign (restrain the affected limb and watch the others): POSITIVE - passive fixation of the hand increases movement in the arm and shoulder
5. variability of amplitude, frequency and axis over the examination: irregular, variable frequency around 4-6 Hz, at times combined with myoclonic jerks
6. video-EEG monitoring with limb surface electrodes: 24 h recording with right-arm surface electrodes: irregular tremor, relatively high frequency with irregularities, no epileptiform correlate
